title: Twins’ Joe Ryan misses start with sore back, putting WBC participation in jeopardy
content:
FORT MYERS, Fla. — Joe Ryan missed Saturday’s start after he was scratched with lower right back tightness, a development that could impact his participation in the World Baseball Classic.

The Minnesota Twins sent their All-Star pitcher to undergo an MRI on Saturday afternoon, but knew little more about his condition. Ryan, who was expected to pitch against the Boston Red Sox, wasn’t available for comment.

“It happened during his prep work,” Twins manager Derek Shelton said. “We sent him for imaging just to be sure. … There is day-to-day soreness with everybody, but this is something that came up.”

A day after Pablo López announced he’d need season-ending elbow surgery, the Twins scratched Ryan without explanation 10 minutes before first pitch. The late announcement led to nervous minutes for Twins fans fearing the worst for Ryan, who not only is the team’s best pitcher, but would also make for an interesting trade chip at the Aug. 3 deadline.

Ryan’s scratch raises questions about whether or not he’d still pitch for Team USA in the WBC next month. Though Ryan needed to be ready earlier in the spring to pitch in the WBC, he said there weren’t many other changes to his offseason preparation.

“It didn’t feel like this crazy overhaul in any way,” Ryan said earlier this month. “We just started things a little bit earlier and let the program and the process take care of the rest.”

Ryan, who threw a live batting practice against teammates on Sunday, is scheduled to join Team USA in Houston at the end of the month.

Royce Lewis homered, singled in a run and stole a base in his spring debut for the Twins, who lost 7-2 to Boston. Simeon Woods Richardson struck out two batters in two scoreless innings pitched. Luke Keaschall tripled and scored.
